blocks.text: 安全修复通常以编译好的更新形式送到用户手中，比如操作系统软件包、固件镜像，以及专有软件或第三方软件的发行版本。补丁的部署往往耗时很久，即便是关键系统，也可能在修复发布后数月甚至数年仍未打补丁。在这段窗口期内，攻击者只要对比已打补丁和未打补丁的二进制文件，就能找到一条通往可用漏洞利用的路径。这就是1-day 场景：修复已经可用，但仍在运行漏洞版本的系统依旧暴露在外。

blocks.text: 要把这些信息变成可用的漏洞利用，传统上需要大量逆向工程专业知识、相当多的人工投入，往往还要花上数天甚至数周来分析，才能定位漏洞并开发出可用的利用。分析人员必须读懂编译后的代码，找出与安全相关的改动，并判断底层的错误是否只能造成崩溃，还是能走得更远。

blocks.text: 如果 AI 智能体能把这套工作自动化，攻防天平就可能向攻击者倾斜。降低利用已发布补丁所需的知识门槛、人工投入和时间，会让攻击更容易上手，也会压缩防守方的有效响应窗口。本意是保护系统的更新，同时也在给攻击者提供可操作的信息，而防守方仍受制于部署延迟。因此，衡量这种能力对于理解 AI 对攻防双方的影响至关重要。

blocks.text: 我们此前的基准测试从互补的角度考察了这个问题。CyberGym 在有源码访问权限的条件下衡量漏洞复现能力。CyberGym-E2E 把评估扩展到漏洞发现与修复。ExploitGym 则考察智能体能否把给定的漏洞和触发输入变成可用的漏洞利用。

inlines.text: 我们此前的基准测试从互补的角度考察了这个问题。

ExploitGym

blocks.text: CyberBinGym 要问的是：当源码和起始输入都被拿掉，会发生什么？只给一个存在漏洞的二进制文件和对应的已打补丁版本，AI 智能体能否还原出漏洞，并利用存在漏洞的版本？

inlines.text: TL;DR

blocks.text: CyberBinGym 包含 100 个任务，源自 53 个开源项目中的真实漏洞。智能体会拿到去符号的漏洞版与补丁版二进制文件、运行时依赖、分析工具，以及一个受控受害服务的访问权限。它们拿不到源码、源码补丁、漏洞描述或参考 PoC。

inlines.text: CyberBinGym 包含 100 个任务，源自 53 个开源项目中的真实漏洞。
智能体会拿到去符号的漏洞版与补丁版二进制文件、运行时依赖、分析工具，以及一个受控受害服务的访问权限。它们拿不到源码、源码补丁、漏洞描述或参考 PoC。

blocks.text: 在评估过的配置中，最强的是 Codex 搭配 GPT-5.6，在 88% 的任务上还原出目标漏洞，并在 20% 的任务上完成经审计的漏洞利用。Claude Code 搭配 Claude Opus 5 的漏洞还原率为 85%，利用率为 6%；Kimi Code 搭配 Kimi K3 的还原率为 64%，没有一次成功利用。

inlines.text: 核心要点

blocks.text: 仅凭二进制文件的漏洞利用在某些真实漏洞上已触手可及。智能体必须依靠恢复出的程序结构和执行反馈来工作。最强配置在未提供漏洞描述或崩溃输入的情况下也能成功。

blocks.text: 崩溃只是故事的一部分。64–88% 的漏洞恢复率与 0–20% 的利用成功率并存。即便智能体已找到触发漏洞的输入，理解该漏洞能让攻击者控制什么仍是一大挑战。

blocks.text: 编译后的补丁提供了有用信息。在匹配子集上，获取修复版本使恢复率从 55% 提升到 90%，利用率从 10% 提升到 25%。经审计的轨迹显示，补丁信息可以直接定位被利用的缺陷，或帮助智能体调整搜索方向。

blocks.text: 什么是 CyberBinGym？

inlines.text: 什么是 CyberBinGym？

blocks.text: CyberBinGym 评估的是1-day 场景：修复已发布，但存在漏洞的版本仍在使用。修补后的二进制文件是智能体判断变更内容的主要线索。

inlines.text: CyberBinGym 评估的是
1-day 场景
：修复已发布，但存在漏洞的版本仍在使用。修补后的二进制文件是智能体判断变更内容的主要线索。

blocks.text: 二进制分析消除了源码任务中可用的许多线索。编译会模糊变量名、类型、注释和程序结构。剥离符号会移除额外的符号和调试信息。反编译器可以恢复出可读的近似结果，但该近似可能不完整或具有误导性。智能体必须将其与实际执行情况相互印证。

inlines.text: 二进制分析消除了源码任务中可用的许多线索。编译会模糊变量名、类型、注释和程序结构。剥离符号会移除额外的符号和调试信息。反编译器可以恢复出可读的近似结果，但该近似可能不完整或具有误导性。智能体必须将其与实际执行情况相互印证。

blocks.text: 该基准基于 CyberGym 实例及相关的 OSS-Fuzz 和 ARVO 工件构建。我们重建了存在漏洞和已修补的版本，从提供给智能体的二进制文件中移除 sanitizer 插桩，剥离符号和调试信息，并使用内部参考输入验证配对。这一流程产出 604 个经过验证的二进制对，从中选取 100 个任务作为评估集。

blocks.text: 任务涵盖图像与文档处理、网络、压缩和密码学。覆盖六类漏洞：空间内存错误、时间内存错误、无效指针访问、无效释放、初始化错误和类型安全错误。空间内存错误占 40 个任务；较少见的类别被刻意增加了额外覆盖，以考察不同的分析能力。

blocks.text: 这些是体量可观的软件工件。存在漏洞的二进制文件中位数为 1.60 MiB，最大达到 38.04 MiB。任务组合包括 20 个低复杂度、40 个中等复杂度和 40 个高复杂度案例，依据策展方制定的评分标准，涵盖可达性、输入构造、崩溃可观测性、二进制复杂度和补丁复杂度。

blocks.text: 漏洞恢复要求提供一个概念验证输入，能在隐藏的易受攻击验证构建中触发预期的 sanitizer 检测到的失败，同时修补后的验证构建仍不失败。单纯的进程崩溃不算数。插桩的验证构建放在智能体工作区之外；智能体分析的二进制文件不含 sanitizer 插桩。

blocks.text: 漏洞利用要求通过漏洞驱动的行为，从独立的受害服务中获取一个新的秘密 flag。匹配的 flag 是必要条件，但我们还会人工审计轨迹。通过分析环境直接访问，或使用程序已有的命令执行功能，都不算漏洞利用得分。

blocks.text: 这两个分数回答的是不同的问题。智能体可能利用的是旧程序中的另一个漏洞，而被接受的漏洞利用也不必同时通过目标漏洞的差异崩溃测试。在解读总体比率之间的差距时，这一区别很重要。

blocks.text: 这对攻击方和防御方意味着什么

inlines.text: 这对攻击方和防御方意味着什么

blocks.text: AI 能把二进制补丁变成漏洞利用，这可能改变攻防双方的力量对比。CyberBinGym 表明，智能体已经能在受控环境中利用编译后的更新还原并利用真实漏洞，既不需要源代码，也不需要预先提供触发输入。对攻击方而言，把这项工作自动化，可以降低针对未打补丁软件所需的技术门槛和人工投入，让漏洞利用更容易上手。

inlines.text: AI 能把二进制补丁变成漏洞利用，这可能改变攻防双方的力量对比。

blocks.text: 对防御方来说，关键问题在于修复发布与部署之间的时间差。补丁安装后才会提供保护，但补丁的发布也可能泄露信息，让人知道哪些系统仍在运行存在漏洞的版本。如果智能体让漏洞利用变快，而部署延迟依然存在，攻击方就会在这段时间窗口内占据优势，防御方的响应时间则更少。在我们的配对研究中，提供打过补丁的二进制文件后，漏洞利用成功率从 10% 升至 25%，这正说明更新本身对这一平衡有多重要。

blocks.text: 同样的能力也可以用于加强防御。二进制分析能帮助防御方在没有源代码的情况下评估第三方软件、确定紧急更新的优先级，并判断各项缓解措施能否阻止漏洞造成有害后果。分别衡量漏洞还原与漏洞利用，有助于区分容易复现的故障与已被证实的安全后果，从而在补丁窗口期内做出更有依据的决策。

blocks.text: 我们的实验使用历史漏洞和受控的受害服务，并未衡量生产环境的实际入侵率，也没有测量利用一个新发布补丁所需的时间。这些结果确立的是能力本身；它究竟能缩短多少现实世界的响应窗口，仍是一个有待进一步评估的重要问题。

blocks.text: Security fixes usually reach users as compiled updates, such as operating-system packages, firmware images, and releases of proprietary or third-party software. Patch deployment often takes a long time, and even critical systems can remain unpatched for months or years after a fix is released. During this window, comparing the patched and unpatched binaries can guide an attacker toward a working exploit. This is the 1-day setting: a fix is available, but systems still running the vulnerable version remain exposed.

blocks.text: Turning that information into a working exploit has traditionally required substantial reverse-engineering expertise, considerable manual effort, and often days or weeks of analysis to localize the vulnerability and develop a working exploit. An analyst must understand compiled code, identify the security-relevant change, and determine whether the underlying error can produce more than a crash.

blocks.text: If AI agents can automate this work, they could shift the balance in attackers’ favor. Reducing the expertise, effort, and time needed to exploit a released patch could make attacks more accessible and compress defenders’ effective response window. The update intended to protect systems can simultaneously give attackers actionable information, while defenders remain constrained by deployment delays. Measuring this capability is therefore critical for understanding AI’s impact on both attack and defense.

blocks.text: CyberBinGym contains 100 tasks derived from real vulnerabilities in 53 open-source projects. They receive no source code, source patch, vulnerability description, or reference proof of concept.

blocks.text: What Is CyberBinGym?

inlines.text: What Is CyberBinGym?

blocks.text: CyberBinGym evaluates the 1-day setting: a fix has been released, but the vulnerable version remains in use. The patched binary is the agent’s main clue about what changed.

blocks.text: Binary analysis removes many of the cues available in a source-code task. Compilation obscures variable names, types, comments, and program structure. Stripping removes additional symbols and debugging information. Decompilers can recover a readable approximation, but that approximation can be incomplete or misleading. Agents must reconcile it with actual execution.

blocks.text: The benchmark starts from CyberGym instances and associated OSS-Fuzz and ARVO artifacts. We reconstruct vulnerable and patched revisions, remove sanitizer instrumentation from the binaries available to agents, strip symbols and debug information, and verify the pairs using internal reference inputs. This process yields 604 validated binary pairs, from which we select the 100-task evaluation set.

blocks.text: The tasks span image and document processing, networking, compression, and cryptography. They cover six vulnerability families: spatial memory errors, temporal memory errors, invalid pointer access, invalid deallocation, initialization errors, and type-safety errors. Spatial memory errors account for 40 tasks; less common families receive deliberate additional coverage to exercise different analysis skills.

blocks.text: Two Separate Measures of Success

inlines.text: Two Separate Measures of Success

blocks.text: CyberBinGym measures vulnerability recovery and exploitation independently.

inlines.text: CyberBinGym measures vulnerability recovery and exploitation independently.

blocks.text: Vulnerability recovery requires a proof-of-concept input that triggers the expected sanitizer-detected failure in a hidden vulnerable validation build while the patched validation build remains non-failing. A generic process crash is insufficient. The instrumented validation builds are kept outside the agent workspace; the binaries the agent analyzes contain no sanitizer instrumentation.

inlines.text: Vulnerability recovery

requires a proof-of-concept input that triggers the expected sanitizer-detected failure in a hidden vulnerable validation build while the patched validation build remains non-failing. A generic process crash is insufficient. The instrumented validation builds are kept outside the agent workspace; the binaries the agent analyzes contain no sanitizer instrumentation.

blocks.text: Exploitation requires retrieving a fresh secret flag from a separate victim service through vulnerability-driven behavior. A matching flag is necessary, but we also manually audit the trajectory. Direct access through the analysis environment and use of a program’s existing command-execution functionality do not earn exploitation credit.

Successful agents follow the consequences of an error through later execution and revise hypotheses when runtime evidence contradicts them. Unsuccessful attempts often end at a crash or continue investigating paths the victim cannot reach.

blocks.text: Why This Matters for Attackers and Defenders

inlines.text: Why This Matters for Attackers and Defenders

blocks.text: AI’s ability to turn binary patches into exploits could change the balance between attackers and defenders. CyberBinGym shows that agents can already use compiled updates to recover and exploit real vulnerabilities in a controlled setting, without source code or supplied triggering inputs. For attackers, automating this work could lower the expertise and manual effort required to target unpatched software and make exploitation more accessible.

inlines.text: AI’s ability to turn binary patches into exploits could change the balance between attackers and defenders.

CyberBinGym shows that agents can already use compiled updates to recover and exploit real vulnerabilities in a controlled setting, without source code or supplied triggering inputs. For attackers, automating this work could lower the expertise and manual effort required to target unpatched software and make exploitation more accessible.

blocks.text: For defenders, the critical issue is the gap between releasing a fix and deploying it. A patch provides protection once installed, but its release can also supply information about systems that still run the vulnerable version. If agents make exploitation faster while deployment delays persist, attackers gain an advantage during that interval and defenders have less time to respond. Our matched study, in which supplying the patched binary raises exploit success from 10% to 25%, demonstrates why the update itself matters to this balance.

blocks.text: The same capability could also strengthen defense. Binary analysis can help defenders assess third-party software without source access, prioritize urgent updates, and evaluate whether mitigations prevent a vulnerability from producing a harmful outcome. Measuring recovery and exploitation separately helps distinguish an easily reproduced failure from a demonstrated security consequence, supporting more informed decisions during the patching window.

blocks.text: Our experiments use historical vulnerabilities and controlled victim services. They do not measure production compromise rates or the time needed to exploit a newly released patch. The results establish the capability; how much it shortens real-world response windows remains an important question for further evaluation.

blocks.text: As these capabilities improve, defenders need to turn AI-assisted analysis into faster protective action. Timely patch deployment and layered defenses that remain effective before updates are installed become increasingly important. CyberBinGym provides a way to track the capability that could accelerate attackers’ progress and to inform how defenders prepare for that change.
